service_boundary: Represents the managed Stability AI API, not Stable Assistant, DreamStudio, downloadable model weights, model licenses, or separately contracted on-premises and self-hosted enterprise deployments.
regional_controls: The reviewed public API documentation does not establish customer-selected processing regions; on-premises and self-hosted enterprise options are separate deployment boundaries.
retention_controls: Inputs, outputs, account data, moderation, and service telemetry are governed by Stability AI's current terms and privacy policy; the reviewed API docs do not support a universal customer-configurable zero-retention claim.
routing: Customers call named Stability endpoints and models; the service is not a cross-provider router.
customization: API parameters cover generation, image-to-image, masks, structure and style control, background and object edits, relighting, and several upscale modes. Enterprise self-hosting is documented separately from the managed API.
strengths: A focused first-party API exposes a deep set of image generation, control, editing, and upscale operations.
Synchronous and asynchronous REST workflows cover both interactive transforms and heavier creative operations.
tradeoffs: The API is specialized for creative media rather than a general text or agent inference catalog.
Public regional and retention controls are less explicit than the feature-level image documentation.
